title: Learning Retrieval Models with Sparse Autoencoders
claim: Retrieval quality depends systematically on which layer the sparse features come from and on dictionary width, with mid-to-late layers and larger widths performing best.
layout: 2 line plots side by side; shared y-axis metric; layer sweep left, width sweep right
description: Two side-by-side line plots, each with a thick black frame, light grid and a legend box in the lower right. Both plots show MTEB(eng, v2) score on the y-axis. The left plot has the SAE layer index (0 to 30) on the x-axis. It has three curves with markers: Llama-Scope with 131k width in teal triangles, Llama-Scope with 32k width in yellow diamonds, and Gemma-Scope with 65k width in red diamonds. All three rise steeply over the early layers and then plateau, at roughly 52-53 for Llama and 49 for Gemma. The right plot has SAE width on a log x-axis, from about 10^4.5 to 10^6. It shows Gemma-2B layer 12 in red circles and layer 19 in yellow squares. Both rise with width, and the layer-12 curve crosses layer 19 near 10^5.4 and ends higher. The eye goes first to the steep red curve on the left plot.
caption: (Left) Performance across layers on Llama Scope (Llama-3.1-8B) and Gemma Scope (Gemma-2-2B). (Right) Performance with increasing SAE width on Gemma-2. Evaluation done with Top-K = (40, 400).
abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) provide a powerful mechanism for decomposing the dense representations produced by Large Language Models (LLMs) into interpretable latent features. We posit that SAEs constitute a natural foundation for Learned Sparse Retrieval (LSR), whose objective is to encode queries and documents into high-dimensional sparse representations optimized for efficient retrieval. In contrast to existing LSR approaches that project input sequences into the vocabulary space, SAE-based representations offer the potential to produce more semantically structured, expressive, and language-agnostic features. Building on this insight, we introduce SPLARE, a method to train SAE-based LSR models. Our experiments, relying on recently released open-source SAEs, demonstrate that this technique consistently outperforms vocabulary-based LSR in multilingual and out-of-domain settings. SPLARE-7B, a multilingual retrieval model capable of producing generalizable sparse latent embeddings for a wide range of languages and domains, achieves top results on MMTEB's multilingual and English retrieval tasks. We also developed a 2B-parameter variant with a significantly lighter footprint.
